text: Flexible endoscopy is valuable for diagnosing small animal gastrointestinal (GI) diseases but requires careful technique to yield meaningful results. This review covers current diagnostic utility, technical considerations for biopsy, optimal instrumentation for mucosal specimen collection, correlation of endoscopic indices with clinical activity and histopathology, and new diagnostic developments. Recent studies established guidelines for the optimal number and quality of biopsy specimens from different gut regions, demonstrated the value of ileal biopsy in diagnosing canine and feline chronic enteropathies, and showed that endoscopic biopsy specimens extend beyond routine hematoxylin and eosin histopathology to immunohistochemical, microbiological, and molecular studies.
